title: The Lesson I Learned From Joseph’s Coat Being Stripped (Genesis 37:23)
paragraphs: The Lesson I Learned From Joseph’s Coat Being Stripped (Genesis 37:23)
They didn’t just strip Joseph of a coat.
They tried to strip him of his identity.
“Then it came to pass, when Joseph had come to his brothers, that they stripped Joseph of his tunic, the tunic of many colors that was on him.” — Genesis 37:23

That coat was a gift from his father.
A sign of favor.
A visible mark that he was loved.
And the first thing jealousy went after was what grace had placed on him.
That hit me hard.

Because sometimes the enemy does not attack your body first.
He attacks your covering.
Your confidence.
Your calling.
Your sense of who God says you are.

Joseph lost the coat before he reached the palace.
He was stripped before he was elevated.
Humiliated before he was honored.
Thrown down before he was lifted up.
And here’s what we miss:
They could remove the coat, but they could not remove the dream.

They touched his garment.
They could not touch God’s purpose.

Maybe that is the lesson for me.
People can misjudge you, betray you, mock what God put on your life, and even take what looked like your advantage.

But if the Lord has spoken over you, no pit can cancel it.
No betrayal can bury it.
No stripping can stop it.
And that points me to Jesus.

Joseph was stripped by jealous hands.
Jesus was stripped by sinful hands.

Joseph was thrown into a pit.
Jesus went to the cross.

Joseph suffered before saving many lives.
Jesus suffered to save our souls.

The Gospel is this:
even when sin shames, wounds, and strips us bare, Christ covers us with something better than Joseph’s coat — His righteousness, His mercy, His grace.

So here is the lesson:
Do not panic when God lets a coat go.
He may be preparing a crown of purpose you could not carry yet.

What people stripped from you may have been painful.
But what Christ is clothing you with is eternal.

Hold on.
The pit is not the end.
The stripping is not the story.
Jesus still rewrites what betrayal tried to destroy.
